hook: ESCAPE ISN'T A CRIME IN GERMANY
youtube_title: Escaping Prison Isn't a Crime in Germany? 🦝⚖️
caption: In Germany, a prisoner's own escape isn't a standalone crime — but helping someone escape is, and the sentence, recapture and any other crimes still apply.
script: Breaking out of prison is not, by itself, a crime in Germany. The catch is everything around it. German criminal law has no offense of simply escaping from custody. The idea goes back to the nineteenth century: a prisoner's urge to be free was treated as a basic human drive, so the escape alone isn't punished. [pause 0.15] But look at section one-twenty of the criminal code. Anyone who frees a prisoner, talks a prisoner into escaping, or helps with the escape faces up to three years in prison. If the helper is an official whose job is to prevent escapes, it's up to five. Even an attempt is punishable. So escaping isn't the crime. Helping is. And the escape doesn't cancel anything. The sentence still stands. The prisoner can be caught and brought straight back, face prison discipline, and hurt their chances of early release. Sawed through the bars? That's property damage. Threatened or hurt a guard? Those are crimes too, and they don't become legal just because they happened during an escape. [loop] So if you ever hear someone say breaking out is legal, just remember
